feedback: Decision: approve. The candidate is the best raced design (iteration 6, score 372.74: kd 0.40, kp 3.0, ki 0.30, base_speed 1.5, sensor x = ±0.032 m, footprint 0.016 m) with one change, kd 0.40 to 0.50. The evidence is iteration 5 to 6, where kd 0.30 to 0.40 raised oval finishes from 7 to 19 of 20 and cut oval line-loss events from 1.2 to 0.25. Iteration 7 showed that base_speed 1.3 cut oval finishes from 19 to 7 of 20 and scored 269.51, while raising s-bend progress only from 0.32 to 0.42 with no s-bend finishes. So speed reduction is rejected, and the candidate restores base_speed 1.5. The candidate is valid: all values are inside the contract, the weights are antisymmetric, and line_loss is last_direction. I make no claim about how it will perform. Kd 0.50 is untested and may over-damp the tightest bends. Read the race as follows. If oval finishes stay at 19 or more and s-bend or slalom progress holds or rises above 0.32 and 0.16, keep kd 0.50 as the new best. If oval finishes fall below 15 or s-bend and slalom progress fall, revert to kd 0.40, which is the best raced design, and do not spend further iterations on kd. In that case the next lever is kp 3.25 at x = ±0.032 m, because kp 3.5 was only tested at the narrower ±0.024 m spread (iteration 2, score 99.25). Keep ki 0.30 and base_speed 1.5 in either case.
requested_changes: Keep base_speed at 1.5 and ki at 0.30. Iteration 7 showed base_speed 1.3 cut oval finishes from 19 to 7 of 20 (score 269.51), so speed reduction is not the lever.

If oval finishes stay at 19 or more and s-bend or slalom progress holds or rises above 0.32 and 0.16 at kd 0.50, keep kd 0.50 as the new best. If oval finishes fall below 15 or s-bend and slalom progress fall, return kd to 0.40 (iteration 6 best).

If kd 0.40 is restored, test kp 3.25 at x = ±0.032 m with kd 0.40, since the earlier kp 3.5 result (iteration 2, score 99.25) came from the narrower ±0.024 m spread and the s-bend and slalom still go off track in every run.
